title: Fade
description: A noodle shop in Kyoto on an autumn afternoon, and the thirty years of sun that come after it. Drag forward and every surface ages by the light it actually receives: the sign and the awning out in the open bleach first, the menu under the awning keeps its colour, the boards go silver and the matte paint chalks. Reds and yellows leave before blue, so the vending machine's red goes pale and the maiko's kimono stays.
intent: Reality pieces, technique 8 (Fade): manipulate a real photograph physically. One photograph is baked into an annual solar dose per pixel (MoGe-2 metric point map; 144 sun directions over a year at 35 N, each with a screen-space depth-march visibility test, clear-sky beam x Kyoto's sunshine fraction, plus sky-view factor x diffuse, at 1/4 resolution on CPU), the photo's own illumination (to recover albedo), and SAM material masks. Live, albedo becomes optical density, split into carbon black and cyan / magenta / yellow dye, each fading exponentially with dose (yellow and magenta about 4x faster than cyan); wood greys, matte paint and fabric chalk. On old Japanese signboards 'only the blue remains': https://www.maru-sin.co.jp/en/news_sanpo/january-2023_01/ ; yellow and magenta process inks are the least lightfast: https://printing.org/content/2018/03/28/a-customer-has-complained-that-a-poster-is-fading-almost-immediately-with-exposure-to
sources: Photograph: 'Traditional Japanese Storefront with Vending Machine' by Pincalo (https://www.pexels.com/@pincalo/) on Pexels, Pexels License (https://www.pexels.com/license/). https://www.pexels.com/photo/traditional-japanese-storefront-with-vending-machine-33163084/ (file: https://images.pexels.com/photos/33163084/pexels-photo-33163084.jpeg, 2374x3561). Cropped to 4:5 (lower 2968 rows), resampled to 1440x1800, a passer-by removed with LaMa (tools/depth/fill.py). Normals, metric depth and sky by MoGe-2 (tools/depth/normals.py); masks by SAM 2.1 (tools/depth/segment.py); maps baked by tools/depth/bakes/fade (prep.py, dose.py, mat.py) into plate.webp, light.webp and mat.webp.
